name: Battle of Magnesia
note: The accounts do not give the compass directions, so the Romans are drawn on the left and the Seleucids on the right. The rivers are placed on the Roman left, where the accounts say the right flank was the one left unprotected. The accounts do not say which Roman formation met Antiochus's attack; the Roman left is used because it stood opposite his right. The Seleucid left wing is drawn as one block although it held many units, and the strengths of both armies are disputed.

terrain.name: Phrygios
terrain.quote: leaving their right flank unprotected by the rivers

units.name: Roman left wing
units.quote: It numbered 10,800 heavy infantrymen drawn from among the Romans and Rome's socii

units.name: Roman centre
units.quote: The center likewise consisted of 10,800 Roman and Latin heavy infantrymen commanded personally by Scipio.

units.name: Roman and Pergamene cavalry
units.quote: The right flank was led by Eumenes and comprised 2,800 to 3,000 cavalry

units.name: Light infantry and archers
units.quote: Ahead of the Roman main force were 3,000 Achaean and Pergamene light infantry and 800 Cretan and Illyrian archers.

units.name: Roman rearguard
units.quote: The rearguard was formed by 2,000 Thracian and Macedonian volunteers

units.name: Roman camp
units.quote: retreating to their camp where they were reinforced by the Thracians and Macedonians

units.name: Seleucid left wing cavalry
units.quote: The left wing of the Seleucid army was commanded by Antiochus' son Seleucus and his nephew Antipater.

units.name: Scythed chariots and camels
units.quote: units of scythed chariots and a unit of camel-borne Arab archers were posted in front of the left flank

units.name: Galatian and other infantry
units.quote: The Galatians, Cappadocians, and mercenary infantry to the left of the phalanx

units.name: Macedonian phalanx
units.quote: The center was formed by a 16,000-strong Macedonian phalanx, commanded by Philip

units.name: Seleucid right wing
units.quote: The right flank was led by Antiochus, consisting of 3,000 cataphracts

units.name: Seleucid camp
units.quote: The war camp was guarded by 7,000 of the least combat-ready Seleucid troops.

phases.title: The armies line up
phases.text: The two armies lined up facing each other without fighting. The Romans stood with their left towards the rivers, and Antiochus took the Roman challenge on the third day after the last Roman advance.
phases.quote: the two armies lined up for battle, without engaging each other

phases.title: Eumenes drives off the chariots
phases.text: Eumenes sent forward archers, slingers and spearmen against the scythed chariots. The chariots suffered heavy casualties and fled in panic, throwing the camel archers and cataphracts behind them into confusion.
phases.quote: Eumenes sent forward his archers, slingers, and spearmen to harass the Seleucid scythed chariots.

phases.title: The Seleucid left is broken
phases.text: Eumenes charged with his cavalry before the cataphracts could reorganise. The Roman and Pergamene cavalry broke through the Seleucid left flank, and the cataphracts fled to the Seleucid camp.
phases.quote: The Roman and Pergamene cavalry broke through the Seleucid left flank, causing the cataphracts to flee to the Seleucid camp.

phases.title: The infantry beside the phalanx give way
phases.text: The Galatians, Cappadocians and mercenary infantry were attacked at once by the Roman centre and right. They retreated, which left the left flank of the phalanx exposed.
phases.quote: faced a simultaneous attack from the Roman center and right, causing them to retreat and exposing the phalanx's left flank.

phases.title: Antiochus attacks and the Roman infantry retreats
phases.text: Antiochus led the attack with the cataphracts and agema cavalry against the Latin infantry, while the argyraspides engaged the Roman legionaries. The Roman infantry broke ranks and retreated to their camp.
phases.quote: Antiochus led the attack with the cataphracts and agema cavalry facing the Latin infantry

phases.title: The Romans are reinforced and rallied at their camp
phases.text: The Thracians and Macedonians reinforced the Roman infantry at their camp, and the tribune Marcus Aemilius Lepidus rallied them. Antiochus's cavalry was unsuitable for taking the camp and became bogged down in the fighting.
phases.quote: Antiochus's cavalry was unsuitable for taking the camp and he became bogged down in the fighting

phases.title: The phalanx holds, then begins to retreat
phases.text: The phalanx held its ground against the Roman infantry but was not mobile enough to dislodge the archers and slingers who bombarded it with projectiles. It began a slow organised retreat.
phases.quote: the Seleucid phalanx held its ground against the Roman infantry

phases.title: The elephants panic and the phalanx breaks
phases.text: The war elephants between the units of the phalanx panicked at the projectiles, and the phalanx broke formation. The phalangites discarded their weapons and abandoned the battlefield.
phases.quote: causing the phalanx to break formation. The phalangites discarded their weapons and abandoned the battlefield.

phases.title: Antiochus withdraws
phases.text: Antiochus's cavalry came back to reinforce the centre after his army had already dispersed. He gathered the surviving troops and retreated to Sardes.
phases.quote: He gathered the surviving troops and retreated to Sardes while the Romans were busy looting his camp.
